prompt: Create one continuous 10-second photoreal novel-view shot of the SAME STATIC physical scene. @Image1 is a real photograph, uniformly scaled and cropped, of the STARTING camera view. It is the authority for object identity, observed construction, materials, colors, lighting, and scene details. It is NOT a character sheet, flat backdrop, or frame to repeat. @Video1 is a procedural geometric reconstruction of that SAME scene. Follow its camera translation, local arc, framing progression, relative depth and changing occlusion. Replace its simplified CG surfaces with the real photographed appearance from @Image1; do not copy low-poly shading or transform the scene into a cartoon. Scene identity: A stationary vintage turquoise flatbed truck viewed from its left-rear three-quarter side. It has weathered turquoise metal, a pale cab, two visible wheels, long brown wooden side boards, rear hinges and tow hardware. Concrete paving, buses, trees, lamps, patio furniture, yellow umbrellas and buildings form the urban background. Camera route: One unbroken 359-degree translated orbit lasting ten seconds. Angular progress is 35.9t + 5.6 sin(4 pi t/10) degrees, never eased to rest. A 32-percent radial pullback, 1.5-unit longitudinal target translation and roughly 2.8-unit elevated middle traverse reveal the bed floor and full opposite side before descending through the front and returning toward the source side. A restrained four-degree middle-lap FOV widening protects the full bonnet and tyre silhouette. Only the camera moves.  KINETIC CAMERA CONTRACT: @Video1 has highest authority for continuous camera motion. @Image1 controls appearance only and must not anchor, slow, recenter or stop the camera. Camera intent: An energetic continuous survey of a fully modeled stationary vintage flatbed, emphasizing rear hinge depth, twin rear tyre spacing, empty plank floor, curved bonnet and both cab faces. Keep moving through the final frame: there is no destination framing, no endpoint hold and no cut. Travel continuously through one 359-degree counterclockwise path over all ten seconds. Screen-space travel: Launch toward the screen-right rear corner; the rear panel broadens as the long visible side foreshortens. Continue around the rear onto the formerly hidden side, swing past the rounded bonnet and front grille, then travel along the original near side. The yellow umbrellas, lantern, truck and foreground manhole travel at distinctly different parallax rates. There is no destination framing and no final hold: every second must contain strong world-space camera displacement, parallax and changing occlusion. Required camera beats: (1) 0-2.5s: Accelerate visually around the screen-right rear brackets while lifting; the rear cross-board unfolds into view and the near tyre moves across the spare. (2) 2.5-5s: Sweep high over the rear corner onto the hidden side while physically dollying outward; separate both timber walls, reveal the complete bed floor and expose far axle components. (3) 5-7.5s: Continue around the far-side cab toward the front, lowering through the bonnet and grille reveal as the tall headboard slips behind the pale roof. (4) 7.5-10s: Dive back toward the original side and tighten the radius, showing wheel-arch, cab-sign and manhole parallax; maintain positive orbit speed through the last frame and complete 359 degrees only at ten seconds. Required changing-occlusion evidence: (1) The narrow right-hand rear cross-board expands to full width between two separated turquoise hinge brackets; the near longitudinal boards then retreat behind it. (2) As the camera clears the far rear corner, the hidden rear wheel pair and far mudflap emerge from behind the spare and chassis while the near rail becomes the far rim of the open bed. (3) The rounded bonnet and pale split windshield move from occlusion behind the tall timber headboard to the foreground during the front traverse; both headlamps and the full bumper separate. (4) The manhole crosses the frame rapidly relative to the wheels, while the twin lantern and yellow umbrellas travel more slowly in the distant patio layer; the newly inferred plaza buildings appear only as the full orbit turns away from the photo-facing facade. Never settle into a hero frame, pause for the action, reverse direction, rotate the subject as a turntable, or replace physical camera travel with digital zoom/pan. Begin at the photographed source composition, then reveal a coherent local novel view with clear foreground/background parallax. Only the camera moves; keep all physical objects and materials fixed. The truck, wheels, wooden bed and all background objects remain stationary. Preserve turquoise weathering, long wooden boards, rear hardware, cab and wheel placement. No driver, pedestrian or other person appears. The real photograph and proxy share the same centered 16:9 aspect-ratio crop. Preserve that crop without stretching, zooming past it, or inventing scene content outside the photographed crop. Complete newly revealed surfaces conservatively from the observed scene; Do not add, remove, morph, duplicate, rotate or animate objects. No cuts, camera jumps, turntable object motion, still-image sliding, text labels or rendered UI.
